items.prompt: Explain the argument of this song as if to a bright 10-year-old. Use ONLY the claims in the ESSENCE list below; every paragraph must correspond to at least one essence item (record indices). Do not add doctrines, comparisons, meta-commentary, or quoted terms. ESSENCE: [0] Mind-wind dissolved in the inward aim; seeing yet not seeing with steady gaze — this is śāmbhavī mudrā by the guru's grace alone: reality free of void and non-void.

paragraphs.text: There is a special locked-in look: your eyes stay open and fixed on the outside world, but your mind and breathing have melted completely inward. You see things and at the same time you do not really see them.

That locked-in look is called the Shambhavi seal, and nobody can force it to happen — it arrives only as a gift from your teacher. And what it opens onto is reality itself: something so free it is beyond both emptiness and fullness.

Use ONLY the claims in the ESSENCE list below; every paragraph must correspond to at least one essence item (record indices). Do not add doctrines, comparisons, meta-commentary, or quoted terms. ESSENCE: [0] Four outer strokes — half-open eyes, steady mind, nose-tip gaze, moon-sun dissolved — then the vision: light-form without exterior, one supreme person attained; after which speech ends.

paragraphs.text: First, four outer details: eyes half open, mind steady, gaze resting on the tip of the nose — and even the inner sun and moon, the energies of day and night, dissolved away.

Then, inside all that quiet, a vision: a human shape made entirely of light, with no outside to it at all. And after that there is simply nothing more to say — the sentence about it ends the way speech itself ends.

Use ONLY the claims in the ESSENCE list below; every paragraph must correspond to at least one essence item (record indices). Do not add doctrines, comparisons, meta-commentary, or quoted terms. ESSENCE: [0] No technique enjoined: whatever sounds is already transcendent mantra, whatever the body postures is already mudrā, whatever the breath's flow is already wonderful yoga — so, in the experienced śākta abode, what would not shine?

paragraphs.text: Here is the whole trick, and it is not a trick you do: any sound that comes out of your mouth is already a sacred word. Any way your body happens to be sitting or standing is already the holy gesture. Any breathing your breath does on its own is already the practice.
So if you are living inside that charged place of awareness, tell me: what in the world would not shine?

items.prompt: Explain the argument of this song as if to a bright 10-year-old. Use ONLY the claims in the ESSENCE list below; every paragraph must correspond to at least one essence item (record indices). Do not add doctrines, comparisons, meta-commentary, or quoted terms. ESSENCE: [0] Each sacred form defined by a vanishing: mantra where letters unnoticed, mudrā where all bodily action dissolved, yoga where breath-flow exhausted — then the festival: for the wise attaining Your abode, everything wonderful.

paragraphs.text: Each holy thing is defined by what drops out of it. A sacred word counts when you stop hearing its letters. A holy gesture counts when every bodily straining has melted away. The practice counts when even the flow of breath is used up.
And then the payoff: for people wise enough to reach that place, everything — absolutely everything — turns out to be wonderful. That is the festival.
